job.title: Secretary | Chief Executive Officer TPAV
job.description:
• Lead Victoria’s influential police representative body
  • Shape outcomes for more than 17,000 members
  • Be a powerful advocate for Victoria’s police and PSO members


About the organisation

The Police Association Victoria (TPAV) is a prominent and trusted voice for more than 17,000 Police Officers and Protective Services Officers across Victoria, representing their industrial, legal and welfare interests. One of the state’s most influential and high-profile representative bodies, TPAV has evolved well beyond its police-union origins. Today, it is multifaceted organisation with around 50 staff and a 12-person Board. The Secretary also serves as Chief Executive Officer of the Victoria Police Branch of the Police Federation of Australia (PFA).


About the role

Reporting to the TPAV Board and working closely with the President, the Secretary (CEO) will lead the organisation in line with its Constitution, plans and policies. Supported by an Assistant Secretary and six-person senior leadership team, you will oversee strategy, finance, risk, member services and business systems. You will lead Enterprise Bargaining Agreement negotiations, manage significant industrial matters and present influential submissions to industrial bodies, Government and senior forums. As TPAV’s principal spokesperson, you will build productive relationships with Victoria Police Command, Members of Parliament, PFA branches and affiliates, the media and relevant lobby groups. Success will be measured by member trust and retention, and by securing the best possible employment terms and conditions for members.


About you

You are a principled, credible and resilient leader with the judgement and presence to represent members in complex, high-profile environments. You bring a contemporary understanding of policing and modern police organisations; operational policing experience is highly desirable. You combine strong industrial negotiation and industrial relations expertise with sound financial and business management skills, including budget preparation and control. A clear, assured communicator, you engage effectively with Government, the media and public forums, remain calm under pressure and build trust across diverse stakeholder groups. Experience in strategic planning, risk management or a membership-based organisation will be well regarded. Self-aware and purpose-driven, you are committed to supporting, advocating for and protecting police members.


How to Apply

For more information and requirements, see the Candidate Brief or to apply, click ‘Apply now’ above, submitting your resume (CV) and a concise cover letter. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK. Closes 9am, 2 November.

job.title: Board Member | Chair of the Board
job.description:
• Non-executive Board leadership role
  • Statewide youth charity since 1976
  • Improve outcomes for young people


About the organisation

Blue Light Victoria (BLV) is a statewide youth charity focused on early intervention and prevention for young people aged 10 to 21. Founded in 1976 commencing with drug- and alcohol-free youth discos, BLV now delivers programs and initiatives to more than 10,000 young people each year. BLV's evidence-based, trauma-informed programs bring young people together with police, emergency services, schools and communities to strengthen belonging, build trusted relationships, improve wellbeing and create safer, stronger communities. The charity is distinguished by its partnerships with police and emergency services, and is guided by the values of Connection, Growth, Innovation and Respect. BLV is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion and child safety.


About the role

BLV is seeking a Director with the capability and aspiration to contribute to the leadership of the Board, with the opportunity to assume the Chair role either on appointment or as part of future Board succession. As a Board member you will contribute to the Board's governance of BLV and its oversight of strategy, organisational performance, impact, financial sustainability and risk, while maintaining clear boundaries between governance and management. For a candidate appointed as Chair, or transitioning to the Chair role in the future, responsibilities will include chairing Board and member meetings, setting agendas with the CEO and Secretary, working with the Deputy Chair on continuity and succession, and leading Board and Director evaluation, renewal and development. The Chair also acts as the primary point of contact between the Board and CEO, leading CEO appointment, goal-setting, performance evaluation, remuneration review and succession planning on behalf of the Board. As a Director, you will also play an important role in representing BLV and strengthening relationships with Victoria Police, government, schools, community partners, funders, donors, branches and volunteers, with a sustained focus on child safety, youth voice, diversity, equity and inclusion. The Director position is a voluntary, non-executive, appointment for a term of up to 3 years, and Chair is for 12 months with eligibility for reappointment at each Annual General Meeting


About you

You are a senior leader with substantial governance experience and a sound understanding of the role and responsibilities of a non-executive Director. Previous Board experience is highly desirable, as is completion of the AICD Company Directors Course or an equivalent governance qualification. You may already have Chair experience or be ready to step into a Chair role, either on appointment or as part of future Board succession planning. You bring strong strategic judgement, financial literacy and an understanding of governance, risk and regulatory oversight, with the ability to assess complex information and guide collective decision-making. Your well-established networks and natural ability to connect people with purpose, will help BLV broaden its funding beyond government sources and support its long-term sustainability. Underpinning your ability to support and work constructively with a CEO and maintain appropriate boundaries between the Board, Chair and CEO, is important, as are your independence, integrity and confidence to challenge constructively. You hold a genuine commitment to BLV's purpose, values, child safety and improving outcomes for young people

 

How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV along with a covering letter. For more information prior to application, please contact Dalia Klein at SHK on 0401 000 499, quoting reference 3693460. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer, Ballarat Foundation
job.description:
• Lead a contemporary community foundation
  • 40-year regional philanthropic institution
  • Enable community-led change, in the region and beyond


About the organisation

For more than 40 years, Ballarat Foundation has connected community generosity with opportunities to strengthen Ballarat and the surrounding region. As a trusted community foundation, it brings together philanthropy, local knowledge, strategic partnerships and community insights to address local challenges and opportunities. Through grant-making, research, philanthropic development, and collaborative initiatives, the Foundation is now entering an exciting new chapter. Building on decades of success, it is evolving its role as a contemporary community foundation strengthening the relationships, capability and knowledge that enable communities to thrive.


About the role

Reporting to the Board, the Chief Executive Officer plays a central role in advancing the Foundation's vision, bringing together people, partnerships and resources to create lasting community impact. Leading strategy, people, operations and finances, the CEO will build strong relationships across the community, philanthropic, business and government sectors while supporting a capable, values-driven team. A key focus will be growing the Foundation's endowment through sub-funds, planned giving and new funding partnerships, ensuring resources are available to support community aspirations for generations to come. The role also oversees grantmaking, community intelligence and research initiatives, including the Vital Signs program, and provides strategic advice to the Board on governance, performance and risk. Success will require a collaborative and influential leader who can connect people around a shared purpose, champion community-led solutions, and turn ideas into meaningful and measurable outcomes.


About you

Passionate about creating meaningful impact in regional communities, you are an accomplished and approachable leader with experience in organisational leadership, governance, financial management and stakeholder engagement. You build trusted relationships across community, government, business and philanthropic sectors, translating opportunities into sustainable outcomes. Collaborative and influential, you communicate with clarity, navigate complexity with confidence, and inspire others around a shared purpose. You will be adept at leading a highly capable, values-driven team and fostering a culture that delivers lasting community impact. Experience in philanthropy, grantmaking, community foundations or related sectors will be highly regarded. Energised by purpose and inspired by community-led change, you are ready to make a lasting contribution as CEO of the Foundation.

job.title: Advancement Programs Director
job.description:
• Leading global university 
  • Shape the future of alumni and donor engagement
  • Build loyalty at scale


About the organisation

UNSW Sydney is a globally connected university with more than 400,000 alumni and a donor community of approximately 25,000. Its strategy, Progress for All, sets an ambitious agenda for creating positive societal impact through education, research and meaningful engagement with its communities and partners. Following a refreshed Advancement strategy, UNSW has created this new role to bring greater strategic coherence to how it engages alumni, donors and supporters throughout their relationship with the University. This is an opportunity to help shape the next phase of an ambitious Advancement function at one of Australia’s leading universities, applying contemporary thinking in loyalty, customer experience, data and lifecycle engagement to a purpose-led organisation with significant scale and impact.


About the role

Reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, and leading a team, the Advancement Programs Director is a key member of the Advancement leadership team, working alongside the Directors of Development, Alumni Experience and Advancement Services to shape a more connected and insight-led approach to alumni and donor engagement. 

The Director will provide strategic leadership for supporter journeys, lifecycle engagement and development communications, including community giving. A central focus will be understanding how different audiences move through the advancement ecosystem, from alumni engagement and community giving through to major and principal gifts, and designing more connected, purposeful experiences along the journey. 

The role will establish the strategies, frameworks and standards that enable consistent communications, events, stewardship and supporter experiences. Working in partnership with Advancement Services, the Director will define the segmentation, data, reporting and insights required to understand audience behaviour, evaluate performance and improvement engagement over time. 

The Director will also represent Advancement audiences and priorities to central marketing, digital and communications teams and senior University leaders. A key early priority will be developing a clear first-year strategy that maps audiences and cohorts, identifies the journeys and experiences required, establishes clear priorities and makes a compelling case for future investment.


About you

Tertiary qualified, you are a senior customer, marketing, or engagement leader with deep expertise in lifecycle strategy, loyalty or CRM-driven engagement, gained in complex organisations. Higher education or philanthropy experience is not essential. You understand how data, insight and customer behaviour can be translated into more meaningful engagement and measurable results. You bring a strong point of view on best practice, can distinguish between what is strategically important and what is simply possible, and are confident setting priorities, including being clear about what not to pursue. You have experience leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing across marketing, digital and data specialists while bringing stakeholders with you through change. You are comfortable operating across a complex institution, building a case for investment and translating strategy into practical action.

You bring curiosity and commercial judgement, along with the confidence to build something new in an environment where ambiguity, competing priorities and limited resources are part of the landscape. What matters is your ability to understand audiences, connect data and experience, build effective strategies and create the conditions for long-term engagement.

Most importantly, you will be excited by the opportunity to build something new and establish the foundations for more connected alumni and donor engagement at scale. 


How to apply

job.title: Head of Digital, Technology and Data
job.description:

  • Four properties, 5,500+ animals
  • Supporting the fight against extinction


About the organisation

Zoos Victoria is a world-leading conservation organisation and Victorian Government statutory authority operating Melbourne Zoo, Werribee Open Range Zoo, Healesville Sanctuary and Kyabram Fauna Park. Welcoming more than three million visitors annually, a paid membership base of over 390,000 and caring for over 5,500 animals, the organisation combines a powerful conservation mission with significant commercial scale and community impact. With ambitious plans for growth and a commitment to creating a future rich in wildlife, Zoos Victoria is enhancing its conservation outcomes, visitor experiences and long-term sustainability


About the role

Based at the Parkville corporate office and reporting to the Chief Finance Officer, the Head of Digital, Technology and Data sets the strategic direction, architecture and delivery of Zoos Victoria's technology, digital systems, business applications and data functions. The Head will develop and maintain the Digital and AI Strategy and is accountable for the Information and Data Protection Framework, cybersecurity, and the reliability of internal and external applications. This includes developing data governance policies, a centralised data management framework, and data literacy across key functional areas to support evidence-based decision making. The Head will also lead business application projects with effective change management, manage functional budgets, and lead a team of 12 (five direct reports) across all four properties. Key to success will be securing ownership of the strategy from the Board, Senior Executive and staff, and making sure initiatives are delivered in a coordinated way with minimal disruption.

 

 About you

Ideally holding graduate ICT qualifications, along with project management certification or equivalent experience, you are a senior digital and technology leader with extensive experience developing and implementing digital strategies in complex stakeholder environments. You have led the strategy and implementation of internal and external customer-facing business applications, and overseen complex project delivery amid ambiguity. You have led accomplished digital and/or IT teams, coached managers to influence stakeholders, and driven organisational change without creating silos. Your background in data analytics, performance reporting and performance measurement supports both operational objectives and the monitoring of strategy. You bring high emotional intelligence, excellent communication and troubleshooting skills, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders on systems and process change.

job.title: Chief Information Officer
job.description:

  • Statewide 24/7 emergency healthcare
  • Enabling best care for Victorians


About the organisation

Ambulance Victoria (AV) brings patient-focused, out-of-hospital, mobile and emergency healthcare to the Victorian community. Operating 24/7 across Metropolitan Melbourne and Regional Victoria, the organisation depends on a secure and resilient technology environment to support its frontline services. AV's Patient Care Commitment is to provide care that is caring, safe, effective and connected for every patient, every time, underpinned by the values of care, accountability, respect and excellence. Within this organisation, technology is positioned as a strategic enabler of service reform, innovation and improved organisational performance.


About the role

Reporting to the Executive Director Enterprise Services, the Chief Information Officer (CIO) holds enterprise-wide accountability for AV's technology, digital and data enablement strategy, and for the performance, security and resilience of its technology environment. The CIO will lead the evolution of a secure, integrated and contemporary technology ecosystem, driving digital transformation, technology modernisation and service improvement across the organisation. This includes technology strategy and architecture, IT service delivery, cyber security, data and AI enablement, and portfolio, investment and vendor management. Working in partnership with clinical, operational and corporate leaders, the CIO will translate organisational priorities into digital capabilities. These will see a modernisation of services, increased interoperability with health, emergency services and government partners, and improved patient outcomes and employee experience. Key to success will be leading organisational and cultural change, ensuring technology investment delivers measurable value, and providing authoritative advice to the CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Board.


About you

You are a commercially astute technology executive with experience leading a large-scale, complex technology function within a highly operational, service-based or similarly multifaceted organisation. Experience in government, health, emergency services, critical infrastructure or another heavily regulated environment will be well regarded. You have led large scale digital and technology transformation and bring strong commercial capability across operating and capital budgets, strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and the management of outsourced and managed services. An inspiring people leader, you build high-performing, accountable and service-oriented teams, and foster a culture in which people constructively challenge existing practices and take accountability for outcomes. Your understanding of cyber security, data, AI and emerging technology, combined with sound strategic judgement, allows you to advise and influence boards and executive leaders on significant technology and investment matters. Tertiary qualified in information technology, computer science, information systems, business or a related discipline (postgraduate qualifications well received), you recognise this a rare opportunity to have state-wide impact.

Central Highlands Water (CHW) is the trusted provider of essential water services to one of Victoria's fastest-growing regional communities. With a clear purpose to deliver safe, reliable and affordable services today and for future generations, CHW is shaping a more sustainable future through its vision of fostering thriving communities, sustainable living and a healthy environment. Reporting to the General Manager, Digital Transformation and Technology Services, the Head of Digital Business Transformation will lead the design, delivery and embedding of CHW's digital transformation programs and projects and is accountable for realising their intended benefits. The Head will also support the development and implementation of CHW's digital and AI strategies, including AI pipelines, business value assessments and governance controls, and will support contributions to the Board and its sub-committees. This leading Australian peak industry body represents a rapidly growing and strategically significant sector, with a membership base spanning major listed corporations through to smaller industry participants. As a not-for-profit, membership-driven organisation, it plays a critical role in supporting and accelerating Australia's energy transition. Its work encompasses policy and advocacy, industry representation, standards and accreditation, market development, and member services, placing it at the intersection of industry, government and the broader community. At a pivotal moment for both the sector and the nation, the organisation is undertaking a deliberate strategic refresh designed to strengthen its impact, enhance member value and reinforce its position as a trusted and influential voice. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary (CFO) leads the organisation's financial strategy, governance and performance. Working closely with the Board and Executive Team, the role provides strategic direction and hands-on oversight of the full finance function, from reporting, budgeting and longer-range financial planning through to statutory compliance, treasury and transactional operations. As Company Secretary, the role coordinates the corporate governance and secretariat function, ensuring statutory, regulatory and constitutional obligations are met, supporting the Board and its Committees, and leading the ongoing review of governance frameworks and instruments. Key to success will be operating as a trusted adviser to the Board, Chair, CEO and Executive Leadership Team on both financial performance and governance matters.

With a footprint that extends across Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Italy, China and India, and comprising more than 20,000 staff and approximately 86,000 students globally, Monash University is Australia's largest and most international university. job.title: Manager, Philanthropy

  • Lead a national major gifts team

About the organisation

This organisation is one of Australia's most recognised and trusted charities operating nationally across every state and territory. With a broad footprint spanning social services, community support, and emergency relief, its operations touch every demographic and age group while also bringing hope to people experiencing hardship and injustice. The organisation serves people across all walks of life — from crisis support to long-term community development. A substantial fundraising operation, underpinned by a high-performing transformational giving team, has delivered consistent year-on-year growth and continues to play a critical role in advancing the organisation’s purpose. About the role

Reporting to the General Manager, Transformational Gifts, the Manager, Philanthropy plays a critical leadership role in advancing the organisation’s mission through the development of meaningful, high-value philanthropic relationships in line with the fundraising strategy. This position is responsible for driving sustainable income growth by identifying, cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major donors including securing seven-figure gifts, and building strong, long-term relationships with philanthropic stakeholders. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on relationship management, the appointee will ensure that philanthropic investment is aligned with organisational priorities and delivers measurable social impact. Collaborating with internal stakeholders to translate programmatic needs into compelling funding propositions, the appointee will build long-term partnerships grounded in trust, transparency and shared purpose, and through disciplined pipeline management, strong market intelligence, and exceptional donor engagement, contribute, to revenue diversification, multi-year funding security, and the overall growth of the philanthropy portfolio. The role is also responsible for achieving financial and non-financial targets, inspiring a national team that is tasked with acquiring new strategic relationships, and driving revenue growth and retention. Critical to success is building team capabilities and optimising ROI performance, while ensuring contemporary best practice processes. 


About you

You are an experienced philanthropy or major gifts leader with demonstrable experience securing seven-figure gifts. You bring leadership experience, ideally across a geographically dispersed team, and possess the commercial and strategic capability to manage a multi ten-million-dollar portfolio of philanthropic revenue. Your stakeholder management skills are well developed, and you present with the gravitas and executive presence required to engage ultra-high-net-worth individuals and their intermediaries. You have the ability to navigate a large complex organisation and to work collaboratively and collectively with this framework. You may come from a large charity, higher education, health or medical research, other relevant philanthropic sectors, or a high-net-worth relationship management background in wealth or private banking where your skills translate meaningfully into the welfare sector. You thrive on operating within a values-led, mission-driven organisation where you can meaningfully impact and transform people’s lives.


How to apply

Click ‘Apply’ to submit your CV. For more information prior to application, please contact Tracy Melonie at SHK via email on tracy.melonie@shk.com.au, quoting reference 3649204. Direct and third-party applications will be forwarded to SHK.
